AI-ConneX

STAGE-WISE INDUSTRIAL VISUALIZATION EXPERIENCE

Data Studio • ML Studio • Agentic StudioJane + Progressive Tabs + Telemetry-Gated VisibilityResearch, POC, Industrial Value & Visualization CatalogueVersion 1.0 | 14 August 2026

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

AI-ConneX should deliberately hide pipeline complexity from industrial users while making the pipeline observable. The user should not have to understand Compiler, Profiler, DAG, recipes, feature pipelines, agent runtimes or model orchestration in order to benefit from them. Instead, Jane is the conversational entry point and each Studio exposes a visual workspace whose tabs progressively unlock as trusted telemetry confirms that a stage has completed.

This is not a 'dashboard for every microservice'. It is a human-understandable digital thread: each tab answers what happened, what was found, why the system made its decision, what evidence supports it, and what is available next. NIST describes visual analytics as analytical reasoning facilitated by interactive visual interfaces and specifically identifies manufacturing benefits including more informed operational decisions, communication across engineering teams, support for less experienced users and multiple lifecycle viewpoints. citeturn0search3

The design principle is: **complexity remains in the backend; evidence becomes visible in the frontend.** Tabs are unlocked by stage telemetry, but unlocking does not mean the user is authorized to perform an operational action. Action permissions remain governed by the platform's tenant, role, policy and approval controls.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 2. Why This Matters to Industrialists | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

NIST's manufacturing visualization research notes that access to data can become overwhelming unless visualization helps humans cognitively integrate information. citeturn0search0

| Industrial problem | Visualization response | Business value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Many data formats / pipelines | Progressive stage views | Understand transformation without learning data engineering |
| Tacit expert knowledge | Visual evidence + explanations | Transfer knowledge to less experienced staff |
| Large heterogeneous datasets | Interactive visual analytics | Find patterns without reading raw tables |
| Model opacity | Mathematical/physical model plots | Understand why a model is useful |
| AI agent opacity | Agent graph + evidence + telemetry | See what the agent knows, decided and did |
| Long-running jobs | Telemetry-gated progress | Know exactly where work is |
| Different departments | Shared visual language | Improve engineering/operations communication |
| No ML use case | Data-only visual route | Still gain operational value from organized data |

[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

The user sees Jane plus the Studio's visual workspace. Internal services remain hidden unless an authorized technical mode is enabled. This keeps the default experience industrialist-friendly.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 4. Tab Unlocking Model | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

Telemetry is therefore a state machine, not merely a progress bar.

| State | Meaning | User experience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LOCKED | Stage has not started or predecessor is not valid | Tab visible but unavailable; shows prerequisite |
| QUEUED | Stage requested | Progress indicator |
| RUNNING | Stage executing | Live telemetry and partial results |
| READY | Stage completed and evidence validated | Tab unlocks |
| WARNING | Completed with material warnings | Tab unlocks with warning badge |
| FAILED | Stage failed | Tab opens diagnostics/retry path |
| STALE | Artifact exists but telemetry is outdated | Shows last known result + refresh |
| SUPERSEDED | A newer run replaced this artifact | History remains accessible |

{  "execution_uid": "EXEC-...",  "tenant_uid": "TEN-...",  "studio": "DATA",  "stage": "PROFILER",  "status": "READY",  "started_at": "...",  "completed_at": "...",  "artifact_refs": ["MANIFEST-..."],  "metrics": {    "rows": 1200000,    "columns": 84,    "quality_score": 0.93  },  "warnings": 3,  "evidence_refs": ["EVID-..."]}

The frontend should unlock a stage only when the backend emits a signed/authorized stage-completion event and the referenced artifact passes validation. Client-side timers must never unlock tabs by themselves.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 6. Common Visualization Interaction Pattern | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

Overview: what happened?

Explore: what does the data/system look like?

Compare: what changed or differs?

Explain: why did AI/pipeline make this decision?

Evidence: which data/telemetry/recipe/model supports it?

History: what happened across runs/time?

Next: what can the user do now?

Every visualization should answer a defined industrial question. Avoid charts whose only purpose is decoration.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 7.4 Mathematical/Physics Layer in Data Studio | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

For datasets where no ML model is required, Data Studio can expose mathematical and physics-derived views: FFT, RMS, variance, rate-of-change, energy proxies, pressure/flow relationships, vibration bands, temperature gradients and domain-specific equations. These are explanatory/analytical layers unless explicitly validated as engineering models.

Vibration → FFT → dominant frequency → possible mechanical signature.

Motor current → RMS/crest factor → load/abnormality indicators.

Pressure + flow → operating envelope visualization.

Temperature → gradient/time derivative → thermal behavior.

Production cycle → cycle-time distribution → bottleneck visualization.

Maintenance logs → text categories + temporal clustering.

NIST has demonstrated visual analytics for heterogeneous machine-maintenance data, including patterns useful for diagnosis and preventive maintenance while retaining a human-in-the-loop. citeturn0search13turn0search8

Managers can understand why the platform recommends ML or a direct data service.

Experienced engineers can use the same visual evidence to validate automated decisions.

Training becomes easier because the system shows the reasoning path rather than only the final artifact.

section: 10. Why Model Plots Matter to Industrialists
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 10. Why Model Plots Matter to Industrialists | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

An industrial model cannot be judged only by one metric. A model can have acceptable accuracy while violating physical expectations, failing under a specific operating regime, or being too expensive/slow for deployment. The Model Plots workspace therefore combines statistical evidence with physical/domain evidence.

Statistical layer answers: 'Is it predictive?'

Mathematical layer answers: 'How does it behave?'

Physical layer answers: 'Does it make engineering sense?'

Operational layer answers: 'Can it run reliably?'

Business layer answers: 'Is it useful enough to deploy?'

This human-centered approach is consistent with research on digital-twin HMI, where visualization and interaction are used to bridge cyber-physical information and human decision-making. citeturn0search18turn0search2

The visualizer must not expose private chain-of-thought. Instead it provides auditable evidence: the user intent, relevant authorized sources, observed telemetry, rules/policies applied, tool calls, approvals, action outcomes and concise reasons. This gives industrialists inspectability without exposing hidden internal reasoning.

USER INTENT   ↓OBSERVED TELEMETRY   ↓AUTHORIZED KNOWLEDGE   ↓POLICY / CONSTRAINT   ↓RECOMMENDATION   ↓APPROVAL (if required)   ↓TOOL ACTION   ↓OBSERVED OUTCOME

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 16. Visualization Design Rules | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

One chart = one primary question.

Always show units, time zone and sampling period for industrial signals.

Show data freshness prominently.

Never imply causality from correlation alone.

Show sample size and confidence/uncertainty where applicable.

Allow drill-down from aggregate to source records.

Preserve engineering units and calibration metadata.

Do not hide warnings behind tooltips only.

Separate measured, derived, predicted and simulated values visually and semantically.

Never mix simulation and live telemetry without an explicit label.

Show last successful telemetry timestamp.

Show data quality beside the visualization.

Provide downloadable evidence/report views.

Use consistent asset IDs and terminology across Studios.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 17. Industrial Safety and Trust Rules | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

Visualization is advisory unless the control path is explicitly authorized.

An alarm visualization must not imply that an alarm has been acknowledged unless an actual acknowledgment exists.

Predicted values must be labeled as predictions.

Physics-derived values must be labeled as calculated/estimated unless validated.

Stale telemetry must be visually distinct from live telemetry.

Agent recommendations must be distinguishable from executed actions.

Action status must be sourced from the tool/industrial system, not inferred by the UI.

All cross-tenant visualization queries must be tenant-authorized.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-020-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Stage Wise Industrial Visualization Experience | Studio: PlatformCore | Category: Visualization | Section: 27. Conclusion | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: VisualizationEngine, PlotlyRenderer, TrendVisualizer]

The proposed visualization layer is strategically important for AI-ConneX because the platform's value is not only that it can automate data engineering, ML and industrial agents. Its value is that an industrialist can understand what the system is doing without becoming a data scientist, ML engineer or agent-runtime specialist.

Data Studio should make the data understandable. ML Studio should make mathematical/model behavior understandable. Agentic Studio should make industrial context, evidence, decisions and actions understandable. The three experiences should be joined by common execution, lineage and telemetry identifiers.

The recommended UX is therefore: **Jane as the conversational guide + stage tabs as the digital thread + telemetry as the unlock mechanism + visualizations as evidence + lineage as the connective tissue + policy as the safety boundary.**
